hints: The friction limit f is the same in both cases. Which block does it drive in each case?
worded:
1. Same limiting friction f = μ m_A g both times.

2. Force on A: B is driven by f, so a = f/m_B and F_A = (m_A + m_B) f/m_B = 9f/5 = 12, giving f = 20/3 N.

3. Force on B: A is driven by f, so a = f/m_A and F_B = 9f/4 = 9 × (20/3)/4 = 15 N. (C)

4. Shortcut: F_B/F_A = m_B/m_A = 5/4, so F_B = 15 N.

**No-pen route: ratio.** F_B/F_A = m_B/m_A = 5/4, so F_B = 12 × 5/4 = 15 N.
conventional:
![](asset:P000570-sol-1)

$$\mu m_{A}g = f,\quad 12 = \left( m_{A} + m_{B} \right)\frac{f}{m_{B}} \Rightarrow f = \frac{20}{3}\unit{N}\ \left( \mu = \frac{1}{6} \right).$$

$$F_{B} = \left( m_{A} + m_{B} \right)\frac{f}{m_{A}} = 9 \cdot \frac{20/3}{4} = 15\unit{N}.$$
mistakes: “Minimum force to make A slip” is the same threshold as “maximum force to move together” with F on A.
